summary: Off-registry HTTP dependency pulls unpinned tarball from non-registry host
details: package.json declares a dependency `ltidisafe` sourced directly from the bare HTTPS URL `https://ltidi.storage.googleapis.com/depenconf/ltidisafe-3.9.8.tgz` rather than from the npm registry. On `npm install`, npm fetches and installs whatever bytes that URL returns, with no registry-side integrity check, no version resolution, and no publisher binding — and executes any lifecycle scripts contained in the fetched tarball. The host is unrelated to any declared repository or homepage for this package, and the implausibly high package version (99.9.1) is consistent with a dependency-confusion / forced-resolution shape against an internal package of the same `fanarena-*` family. The manifest alone is the attack surface: regardless of the current contents of the remote tarball, the publisher of that URL can change the bytes installers execute at any time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
